Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Embracing Change and Letting Go.
You know, a living relationship with God isn’t something that stands still. It grows, shifts, and adapts as life itself changes—whether that’s stepping into a new season, facing challenges, or grabbing hold of unexpected opportunities. The way you experience God’s presence is meant to evolve too. And honestly, being open to that kind of fluidity? That’s the real secret to growing deeper.
Of course, letting go can be tough. It’s normal to cling to old routines or expectations, especially when they’ve worked in the past. But think about a tree in autumn—it lets go of its leaves, not because it’s giving up, but to make space for fresh growth. In our spiritual lives, it’s the same story. Sometimes, the best thing we can do is loosen our grip on what used to fit, and make room for what’s next.
So, how do you actually embrace change? There are a few guiding principles that might help:
First, regularly reassess your spiritual practices. What worked last year, or even last month, might not fit where you are today. It’s okay to adapt to what you need right now.
Second, let go of any guilt or frustration if your routines fall apart or shift. Life happens. Sometimes, things just change.
And most importantly, trust that God’s presence isn’t tied down to any one ritual or routine. God can meet you anywhere, in any moment.
This kind of flexibility opens the door to creativity and resilience. Imagine starting a new job, moving to a new place, or navigating changes in your family. It might throw your established routines out the window, but that’s not a setback—it’s actually an invitation. An invitation to find new, sometimes unexpected, ways to connect.
Take a parent with young kids, for example. Quiet mornings for prayer might be a distant memory. But those moments of connection with God? They can slip in during playtime, bedtime stories, or even in the middle of all the noise. Or maybe you’re going through illness or loss. Sometimes, what matters most isn’t a long, quiet reflection, but a simple prayer or the comfort of a supportive community.
Embracing change also means letting go of the need for control—or always knowing what’s next. Spiritual life isn’t a project you manage; it’s a relationship you live. There’ll be clear days and confusing ones, times when you feel full and times when you feel empty. Every season has its own lessons and gifts, even if they’re hard to see at first.
So, what’s the heart of it all? Embracing change is really about trust. Trusting that God walks with you, no matter how much the landscape shifts. And that kind of trust frees you—to step forward with courage, curiosity, and hope, no matter what comes next.
